episodes.title: 43 Years of Marriage. Evicted with Five Children.

blocks.text:
Indore, 1975. 62-year-old Shah Bano Begum was driven out of her matrimonial home by her husband, Mohd. Ahmed Khan, a renowned and wealthy advocate.

After 43 years of marriage and raising 5 children, she found herself with zero income and nowhere to turn.

FACTUAL MATRIX (Statement of Facts): Indore, 1975. 62-year-old Shah Bano Begum was driven out of her matrimonial home by her husband, Mohd. Ahmed Khan, a renowned and wealthy advocate.

After 43 years of marriage and raising 5 children, she found herself with zero income and nowhere to turn. The legal controversy originated from whether the act committed fell within the statutory exceptions.

episodes.title: The Claim: ₹500/month. The Defense: Instant Triple Talaq.

blocks.text:
In April 1978, Shah Bano filed an application under Section 125 CrPC claiming Rs. 500 per month for maintenance.

In November 1978, the husband pronounced irrevocable Talaq, deposited Rs. 3,000 as Dower/Mehr, and argued he was completely discharged under Islamic law.

episodes.title: 23 April 1985: Section 125 CrPC is Secular and Universal.

blocks.text:
A unanimous 5-judge Constitution Bench led by CJI Chandrachud held:

**"Section 125 CrPC is a secular provision designed to prevent destitution. It cuts across the barriers of religion and applies equally to all wives, children, and parents."**

The court ordered the husband to pay maintenance, establishing gender justice as a paramount constitutional principle.

episodes.title: The Danial Latifi Precedent: Enduring Protection.

blocks.text:
Although the subsequent 1986 Act attempted to restrict Section 125, the Supreme Court in **Danial Latifi v. Union of India (2001)** interpreted the law to require husbands to make a "reasonable and fair provision" for the wife’s ENTIRE life within the Iddat period.

Shah Bano’s courageous crusade laid the bedrock for modern gender equality in Indian family jurisprudence.

flashcards.q: Which court decided The Shah Bano Case and in what year?
flashcards.a: Supreme Court of India in the year 1985.

flashcards.q: What was the primary legal issue addressed in this case?
What is the core Ratio Decidendi of the judgment?
flashcards.a: A unanimous 5-judge Constitution Bench held that Section 125 CrPC is a secular social-welfare provision that applies to all citizens irrespective of religion. A divorced Muslim woman unable to maintain herself is entitled to maintenance from her former husband.

flashcards.q: What is the primary citation for this ruling?
flashcards.a: Mohd. Ahmed Khan v. Shah Bano Begum, (1985) 2 SCC 556, AIR 1985 SC 945

flashcards.q: What is the current legal status of this precedent?
flashcards.a: Section 125 CrPC applicability to Muslim women was modified by 1986 Act, then harmonized in Danial Latifi (2001).

affectsYou.heading: कानूनी निष्कर्ष
points: अदालत का फैसला निचली अदालतों के लिए बाध्यकारी है।

timeline.event: Supreme Court holds Section 125 CrPC applies universally to divorced Muslim women.
Parliament passes Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act 1986.
Danial Latifi v. UOI upholds 1986 Act by interpreting reasonable and fair provision to cover entire life.
Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act criminalizes instant Triple Talaq.

subsequentHistory.note: Affirmed and applied in subsequent landmark jurisprudence.
